newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares go into Xmas week in festive mood.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares go into Xmas week in festive mood.

text.p: South African shares will enter the Christmas season in a festive mood with those traders not on holiday snapping up bargain shares in a market seen as oversold, portfolio managers said on Friday.
The seasonal Christmas hangover came early for South African share watchers with Tuesday's December contract futures close-out sparking a sell-off that left prices battered and bruised.
However, the market has bounced since then and most portfolio managers expect a good Christmas week -- despite Wednesday and Thursday being official holidays.
Wall Street, which on Thursday saw its second biggest ever points rise, should keep the upward impetus in South African equities going until the New Year.
"The market has bounced now and that should carry on next week," said one portfolio manager who declined to be identified.
But many stocks are still reeling from the sell-off and look cheap. Fund managers said there should be healthy, if selective, buying interest next week.
"There are certain companies that are bargains. They were oversold and now they look cheap," the portfolio manager said.
But with many market figures forsaking the dealing floor for the beach, trade will be thin and the market could be volatile and vulnerable to manipulation.

"Some institutional portfolios have been really hammered and when the market gets thin it is certainly an opportunity to jig up prices. There are already signs of it happening," said Denzil Newman, portfolio manager at Syfrets Managed Assets.
But despite expectations of a rising trend emerging in the South African market there is little sign of a fundamental recovery in the value of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE).
Since setting a record trading high of 7,099.4 on October 15 the JSE has slipped badly. At 0940 GMT the all-share index was 6,508.8, up 40.8 on the day.
"There is quite good value in some shares, but there won't be any ongoing revaluation of the whole market," Newman said.

Investec Asset Management portfolio manager Andre Joubert said that the negative sentiment that has dogged the market in the last few months of 1996 was still prevalent and would provide a cap to any gains over Christmas and the New Year -- whatever the performance of New York shares.
"Despite what happens on Wall Street the underlying negative sentiment will prevail," he cautioned.
